newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK non-EU and global trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK non-EU and global trade data.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to UK trade data published at 0830 GMT.

The figures showed July's non-EU trade deficit totalled 506 million stg while June's whole world deficit was 1.12 billion stg. Market forecasts were for a non-EU deficit of 900 million stg and a global deficit of 1.4 billion stg.
"The latest non-EU data will be the main focus and seem to imply that the trend is still looking quite favourable with export growth at least keeping pace with import growth."
"But to be tinkering around with interest rates on the downside now would look increasingly to the markets like a final political gesture. It would perhaps go down badly." (RFTV)

"The July figures are pretty encouraging, certainly much better than had been expected. They tend to suggest that there's been some improvement in the export outlook which was what the CBI seemed to be suggesting in their quarterly survey. The Chancellor will be looking fairly favourably at the numbers. There have been some indications of consumer spending picking up. Normally, that would be associated with higher imports. The best we can hope for is for some stability. It's likely we will see some deterioration in the second half of this year."

"A bit static at the whole world level but there's a bit of a surprise with the non-EU. It's broadly half the level that it has been in recent months. I still think the deficit will deteriorate as consumer spending picks up but sterling's got a bit of a boost from the figures. It augurs well for third quarter GDP."
